findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, truncated file)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted filesystem input can abort the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on malformed input (missing second field or non-numeric value)
findings.failure_mode: corrupt or truncated session file can panic the caller instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use parts.get(1).ok_or(MalformedRecord) and handle parse failure with map_err to a domain error

findings.problem: lossy `as u16` cast from u32 truncates values outside 0..=65535 silently
findings.failure_mode: values > 65535 wrap around silently producing invalid Records with no indication of data loss
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ValueOutOfBounds) or check range with .is_ok() / .is_err()

findings.problem: split(',') + collect() into Vec instead of split_once for two-field CSV grammar
findings.failure_mode: allocates a full Vec of all split parts when only two fields are needed; also silently ignores lines with extra commas, masking data quality issues
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to extract name and value parts directly, handling the Some/None case

findings.problem: unchecked indexing parts[1] after split — line may have fewer than 2 comma-separated fields
findings.failure_mode: malformed input (e.g. single field line "foo") panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: use .get(1) or destructure the split_once result to handle missing fields explicitly

findings.problem: println!() side effect inside pure-looking parsing function
findings.failure_mode: hidden I/O breaks purity of the parsing pipeline; makes the function non-deterministic in output and untestable without capturing stdout
findings.fix: remove println! or move logging to the shell layer; return data-only from the core function

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no try_reserve or bounded capacity handling
findings.failure_mode: maliciously large file triggers unbounded heap allocation; allocation failure is not handled, leading to OOM or panic
findings.fix: use try_reserve on the Vec with a configurable maximum capacity, handling AllocationError

findings.problem: no benchmarks, profiler data, or allocation evidence exist for the load_sessions hot path
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify that the split/collect pattern, println! call, or allocation strategy are optimal for the target workload
findings.fix: add criterion or custom benchmarks measuring throughput and allocation count for representative input sizes
